Action Plan:
1. Acute diarrhoea with abdominal pain/vomiting – likely gastroenteritis:
   • Increase oral fluids (water ± oral rehydration solution) to replace ongoing losses.  
   • Monitor for red-flag symptoms (fever, blood in stool/vomit, worsening pain, inability to keep fluids down).  
   • Remain at home/off work until symptoms improve.  
   • Avoid empiric antibiotics at this stage.  
   • If condition worsens or persists > 24–48 h, attend in-person GP review for abdominal examination and possible further investigations.  
2. Family history of bowel cancer – patient anxiety:  
   • Reassured that current presentation is most consistent with infectious gastroenteritis, not bowel malignancy.  
   • Advised follow-up with regular GP if gastrointestinal symptoms persist, recur, or if additional alarm features (weight loss, rectal bleeding) develop.  
3. Asthma:  
   • Continue usual inhaler (brand change acceptable); no indication that inhaler is causing current symptoms.  
   • Seek medical review if any deterioration in respiratory control.  

Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 3-day history of diarrhoea associated with central abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting.  
• Course: Neither improving nor worsening; needs toilet frequently (urgent, recurrent stools every ~10 min).  
• Associated symptoms: Mild nausea, abdominal gurgling, mild tenderness; denies blood in stool or vomit; reports sweating but no clear fever.  
• Triggers: Uncertain; denies obvious food trigger; wonders if new inhaler brand related.  
• Past medical history: Asthma.  
• Medications: Inhaler for asthma (brand/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: NKDA stated.  
• Family history: Father died of bowel cancer (~10 years ago).  
• Social: Unable to attend work due to frequent stools; otherwise not detailed.

Objective:
• No formal vitals recorded.  
• Patient-reported findings: Mild central abdominal tenderness on self-palpation; able to walk/talk; no chest pain; baseline asthma control unchanged.  
• No investigations performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhoea with abdominal pain/vomiting  
   - Assessment: Gastroenteritis (infective), most likely food-borne/viral.  
   - Differential: Food poisoning, viral gastroenteritis, less likely inflammatory bowel disease or medication effect.  
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; consider stool culture or bloods if symptoms persist/worsen (to be arranged by GP).  
   - Treatment planned: Oral hydration, symptomatic care, watchful waiting, no antibiotics at present.  
   - Relevant referrals: In-person GP review if deterioration or no improvement within 24–48 h.

2. Family history of bowel cancer  
   - Assessment: Patient anxiety regarding hereditary risk.  
   - Investigations planned: Not at this time; consider age-appropriate bowel cancer screening at GP if symptoms persist.  
   - Treatment planned: Education/reassurance.  
   - Relevant referrals: GP follow-up for risk assessment and potential screening discussion.

3. Asthma (stable)  
   - Assessment: Chronic asthma, currently stable.  
   - Treatment planned: Continue current inhaler; ensure adequate supply.  
   - Relevant referrals: None at present.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: No vitals (temperature, BP, HR), no full medication list, smoking/alcohol history not elicited.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient uncertain about presence of blood in vomit, then clarified likely strawberries – conflict noted and resolved.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional pauses/over-talk, but clinically adequate.
